6805 bearing support

Independent assembly · 4 mm wall · Existing 40 mm travel screw + bearing ring

100%

Cap, circlip, bearing, motor and screw separate in stages. Circlip expansion is illustrative; this is not a force simulation.

The bearing carries axial load into the wall. The existing D-shaft clamp remains accessible through the open holder.

6805
4mm
24.2mm
2

Support the screw independently of the motor coupling

The load path is screw → printed shoulder or steel circlip → bearing inner race → bearing outer race → holder → wall. The removable cap captures the outer race, while a narrow spacer keeps the circlip load on the inner race. Open sides leave room to fit and tighten the original coupling.

Existing screw + one added ring

The original helix, D bore, clamp slit and bolt/nut pockets are retained. The added ring includes a Ø24.9 mm journal for the 25 mm bearing bore, a Ø27 mm shoulder and a DIN 471 circlip groove. It occupies X26.2–39.3 mm.

Separate prototype

The motor and screw keep their existing relative positions. The wall is 52 × 52 × 4 mm. This assembly contains no carriage and does not change the existing actuators. The new ring covers the first 9.3 mm of the helical region, so this is not a drop-in carriage retrofit.

Positive retention

Use a purchased spring-steel DIN 471 circlip for a 25 mm shaft. The holder’s bearing pocket is Ø37.2 mm, with 0.2 mm axial allowance. Fit and shim against the appropriate race; do not clamp the bearing shields. PETG groove strength and vibration retention still need physical testing.

Geometry checks

Loading validation…

All 35 sampled exploded-assembly poses are free of solid intersections. The circlip expands before withdrawal. Sampling checks rigid clearances; it does not model deformation forces.

The intended load is about 1 lb (4.45 N static), not a tested capacity. CAD checks do not establish creep life, fatigue, press-fit forces or vibration resistance. Bearing internals and circlip shape are reference envelopes. This bearing does not prevent back-driving when the motor is unpowered.

Geometry report · Assembly pose report

Assembly and hardware

  1. Load the four cap nuts, then attach the holder and 4 mm wall to the motor with four M3×16 screws. Verify the motor accepts 6 mm thread engagement.
  2. Fit the original clamp nut and bolt, then slide the screw onto the D shaft with the clamp loose.
  3. Slide the 6805 bearing over the screw into its pocket and against the shoulder. Add the inner-race spacer and install the steel circlip with circlip pliers.
  4. Fit the cap with four M3×12 screws and nuts. Tighten the coupling through the open holder, then check free rotation, axial play and full circlip seating.

Print the wall and cap flat; print the holder with its cap face on the bed and standoffs upward. Check actual PETG fits before loading the prototype. Full build notes and hardware list.

Dimensions: NSK 6805 · DIN 471-25 circlip.
